summary: Build data contracts, govern data products, and scale reliable self-service analytics. Explore the practical course and enrol your team.
lede: Data contracts and data product governance help experienced data professionals set clear expectations for shared analytics products. The course covers defining versioned schemas and consumer promises, setting measurable quality checks, and linking ownership to catalogue metadata and lineage. Participants also practise reviewing schema changes and preparing governance decisions for domain teams.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for experienced data professionals who must connect domain ownership, engineering controls, and governance decisions across complex analytics environments. It suits teams moving from introductory data mesh or governance concepts toward practical data product accountability and contract enforcement.
modules: Data Product Design and Service Management
prerequisites: You should have practical experience with data architecture, data engineering, business intelligence, analytics platforms, or data governance. Working knowledge of relational data, SQL, metadata, data quality, and distributed delivery workflows is expected. Basic YAML or JSON reading is useful, but programming is not required for completion. Advanced topics such as policy-as-code, event-driven contracts, and AI-assisted quality monitoring are taught at operational application and conceptual awareness levels rather than production engineering depth. Bring examples of recurring data quality issues, unclear ownership, or schema-change problems from your environment if permitted by your organisation.
